accepted_answers.name: Celery
accepted_answers.why: Default for large/heterogeneous workloads: multi-broker, routing, canvas workflows, Celery Beat scheduling, Flower monitoring.

accepted_answers.name: RQ
accepted_answers.why: Accepted default for simple sync jobs on Redis: minutes of setup, inspectable dashboard, handles ~80% of web-service cases.

accepted_answers.name: Dramatiq
accepted_answers.why: Accepted when reliability semantics matter with low ceremony: sane retry/dead-letter defaults, clean middleware.

accepted_answers.name: ARQ
accepted_answers.why: Accepted for asyncio-native apps with I/O-bound jobs.

notes: No single winner: consensus is a decision tree (async -> ARQ; simple sync -> RQ; reliability-first -> Dramatiq; complex/scale -> Celery). A custom threads-plus-list queue is never the answer once durability/retries matter.
problem: Running background jobs in Python with a hand-rolled thread pool and in-memory list.
